model: DULCOMETER diaLog DACb multi-parameter controller (Modbus RTU)
applies_to: diaLog DACb controllers with the Modbus RTU interface option, per software manual BA DM 232 01/19.
summary: The diaLog DACb is ProMinent's multi-parameter measuring and control controller with up to three measuring and control channels plus a calculated (mathematic) channel. With the Modbus RTU option it is an RS-485 or RS-232 slave. This map covers the measured values, setpoints, status, warning and error words per channel, output states, device information, stop/pause commands, the per-channel control configuration (setpoints, limits, PID terms) and calibration values.

source.title: Software manual DULCOMETER Multi-parameter controller diaLog DACb Modbus RTU
source.pages: pp. 4-8 (settings, commands, word order, numbering), pp. 8-12 (register table), pp. 13-17 (bit fields)

addressing.note: The manual prints a decimal 'Register' number plus the hex PDU address; the PDU address is the register minus 1 (register 100 is requested at PDU address 99, hex 63). The 'address' field here is the PDU address.

notes: 32-bit values (FLOAT32 and UINT32) put bits 31-16 in the first register and bits 15-0 in the second, so the word order is ABCD; bytes are sent high byte first. Register 198 (PDU 197) always reads 0xAABBCCDD as a check.
Measured value, setpoint, limits and Xp are floats in whatever unit the channel is configured for (pH, mV, ppm and so on); the manual does not list units for them.

Left out: Pump relay 4 (register 139), because its printed PDU address (hex 90) does not match register 139 (which would be hex 8A); the identity-code registers 150-161, because their text encoding is not described; the math-channel error registers 130/131, which the manual marks as reserved for later use; and channel 1 'Additive basic load' (215), printed as UINT16 although its range is -100 to +100 % (channels 2 and 3 are INT16).
Channel 1 temperature is printed as INT16 and the other channels' temperature as UINT16; both are in 0.1 °C steps and are listed exactly as printed.

Configuration word bits 3-6 (channels 1 and 2 only, valid only when bit 15 = 1) hold the control type: 0 off, 1 manual, 2 P one-way increase, 3 P one-way decrease, 4 P two-way standard, 5 P two-way dead zone, 6 PID one-way increase, 7 PID one-way decrease, 8 PID two-way standard, 9 PID two-way dead zone.
Left out: registers 291 and 293, which the manual labels 'Slope Channel 1' and 'Zero point Channel 1' a second time (probably channel 3).
The text of section 1.7 calls the byte-order test register 'Register 199', but the register table prints it as register 198 (PDU hex C5); the table value is used here.

integration.summary: Read holding registers (function 03) from PDU 99: each channel block gives the measured value and setpoint as floats followed by status, warnings and the 32-bit error words. Check the endian test value at PDU 197 first. Writes use function 06 for single registers and 16 for floats.
integration.enable: Set the slave address, baud rate, serial format, interface mode and termination in SETUP > BUS configuration (access code needed). Bus control parameters are used when bit 15 of the channel configuration word is set.
quirks: Register numbers are 1-based; subtract 1 for the PDU address.
Byte-sized parameters use only the low 8 bits of the register; write the top 8 bits as 0.
If one register in a multi-register write raises an exception, the rest of that write is ignored.
setup: Factory settings: RS-485, slave address 1, 19200 baud, 8 data bits, odd parity, 1 stop bit; termination off.
Turn on active termination in the menu when the controller is the last device on the RS-485 line.
With no parity, 2 stop bits are required.
gotchas: Keep responses short at low baud rates: the manual warns that replies over about 100 bytes at 9600 baud (200 at 19200) may be corrupted.
Read-only registers answer only to function 03.

address_note: address = 0-based Modbus wire (PDU) address; documented = as printed in the source.
